solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: With no waiting in line, chain store's popular

parts.note: IKEA is the Swedish furniture chain; with its 's that gives IKEAS
something hot is in demand, popular

explanation.surface: A shopper hears that a chain store is so popular there is no queue to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: IKEA, the flat-pack furniture retailer, is the chain store; 'in' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something like a shot is to do it instantly, without any delay at all.

clue.text: Group of stars holding cape's clingy fabric

indicators.note: the constellation's name holds the abbreviation inside it, like hands around an object

parts.note: Lyra, the Lyre, is a constellation
C is the map abbreviation for cape

explanation.surface: An astronomer notes a constellation wrapped in a cape made of stretchy material.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is the trade name of a stretchy synthetic fibre used for close-fitting sportswear.

clue.text: King heading off cause of malfunction in government

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: the gremlin loses its head, so its first letter goes

parts.note: a gremlin is the imaginary imp blamed for mechanical faults

explanation.surface: A monarch sees off the source of trouble in his administration.
explanation.walkthrough: A gremlin is the imaginary imp blamed for machines going wrong, a term from RAF slang; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin, the Moscow citadel, is used by metonymy for the Russian government.

clue.text: Seaman, say, hemmed in by land is giving up

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

indicators.note: the abbreviation is surrounded by the word for land as if fenced in

parts.note: a nation is a country, a land
EG, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: A sailor stranded inland, surrounded by land, decides to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: AB, able seaman, stays outside: only 'say' is hemmed in by the land word. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnegation is self-denial, the renouncing or surrender of something one wants.

clue.text: Pack squirrel away that's been caught?

indicators.note: caught by the ear: what was heard, so the word is entered by its sound

parts.note: to squirrel something away is to hoard it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the creature that stashed nuts has been trapped by the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: HOARD and HORDE sound alike in most accents.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd or band, much like a pack of people or animals.

clue.text: Fix pocket on the bottom of legwear

indicators.note: in a down entry the pot word sits underneath the legwear word

parts.note: tights are close-fitting legwear
to pot a ball in snooker is to pocket it

explanation.surface: A tailor is asked to repair a pocket sewn at the seat of some leggings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a fix is being in an awkward predicament, a tight spot.

clue.text: Time to get into bubbly musical work

indicators.note: the time letter goes inside the champagne

parts.note: Moët is a brand of champagne, informally bubbly

explanation.surface: Time to open the champagne for a musical performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral composition, usually sacred and polyphonic.

clue.text: Either end of musician or poet's early period

indicators.note: an end of the word musician is wanted, here the front one, before the conjunction

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: either end serves, so the back end of musician follows the conjunction too

explanation.surface: A literary critic considers either the musician's or the poet's early career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either end' supplies both ends, the first in front of OR and the last behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Morn is a poetic word for morning, the early part of the day.

clue.text: Incredible tact in entertaining one liner

indicators.note: the jumbled letters play host to the numeral, holding it inside
an incredible version of the letters is an unbelievable reworking of them

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cruise passenger marvels at the diplomacy shown while hosting aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: TACT IN is rearranged as TITANC, with I placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titanic was the famous ocean liner that sank on its maiden voyage in 1912.

clue.text: Stuffing starter of turkey with mix ready for cooking

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter only

indicators.note: ingredients prepared for cooking are mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook prepares turkey stuffing with a ready-made mix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing' looks like the Christmas dish but means preserving animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxidermy is the craft of preparing and mounting animal skins over a filling, i.e. stuffing dead creatures.

clue.text: Charlie having successfully dieted daily?

parts.note: C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
someone who has dieted well is now leaner

explanation.surface: Charlie has slimmed down by dieting every day.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a daily is a domestic help who comes in each day to clean; the question mark flags this sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is British slang for a household cleaning lady who comes in every weekday.

clue.text: Obtain old clothing if not waterproof material

indicators.note: the word for obtain and the former word dress the conjunction, wrapping round it

parts.note: to obtain is to get
or means otherwise, if not
EX is a prefix meaning former, old

explanation.surface: Buy old clothes unless they are made of waterproof fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' is a verb here: the obtain and old words dress the 'if not' word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore-Tex is a breathable, rainproof membrane fabric used in outdoor jackets and boots.

clue.text: Instruction for player — left winger, perhaps, entering pitch

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the pitch word

parts.note: alto is a vocal range, a pitch
an egret is a bird, one example of something with wings

explanation.surface: A football manager tells a left winger to come on to the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' and 'pitch' suggest football; the winger is a bird and the pitch a voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegretto is a tempo marking on a score telling a musician to play fairly briskly.

clue.text: Girl India put in goal

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the goal word

parts.note: an end is an aim, a goal
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A girl from India scores, putting the ball in the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female given name, as in the children's writer Enid Blyton.

clue.text: Just two different forms of golf for entertainment

parts.note: fair means just, equitable
G is golf in the NATO alphabet, and a round is a game of golf

explanation.surface: Fair play: two kinds of golf are offered for amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: The two forms of golf are G and ROUND; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is an open site with rides and stalls, a place of amusement.

clue.text: Artist performing in opera company

indicators.note: the performing word goes inside the company's short name

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Opera of New York
a performer who is on is on stage

explanation.surface: An artist is appearing on stage with an opera company.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter of the water lilies series.

clue.text: Bird between two big roads in heat

indicators.note: the bird sits between the two road names

parts.note: M1 (written MI) is Britain's first motorway, and AVE is short for avenue
a crow is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird stranded between two major roads during a heatwave.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To microwave food is to cook or warm it in a microwave oven, so it means to heat.

clue.text: Maybe one with elan stripped off and pranced exotically?

definitions.text: Maybe one with elan stripped off and pranced exotically?

indicators.note: with its outer layer peeled away, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the middle letters only

indicators.note: an exotic version of the letters is a strange rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who stripped with flair and danced in an exotic manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' signals that the whole clue also paints the performer: someone stripping and dancing with flair.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap dancer is an erotic performer who strips and dances close to a seated customer.

clue.text: Punishes breaking into fields having much greenery

indicators.note: the punishing word forces its way inside the fields

parts.note: leas are meadows, fields
to fine someone is to punish them

explanation.surface: Penalties for trespass into lush green fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafiness is the quality of having abundant foliage, lots of leaves and green growth.

clue.text: Harmonious, exclusive component of hymns and rhythms?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in music, in agreement, not discordant

definitions.text: exclusive component of hymns and rhythms?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a letter that is not a vowel; HYMNS and RHYTHMS contain nothing else

explanation.surface: Musically pleasing, the sole ingredient of church songs and beats.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are spelt without A, E, I, O or U, so their letters are consonants only.
explanation.definitionFit: Consonant describes sounds in agreement, and as a noun is a non-vowel letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: What may go on after retiring in close game

definitions.text: What may go on after retiring

parts.note: nigh means near, close
a tie is a match, a game, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: A tense finish: what happens after a player withdraws from a tight match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' means going to bed, not quitting the game; 'in' is a link. A cup tie is a British knockout match.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, put on when one goes to bed for the night.

clue.text: Wanting practice in game enclosure

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: Out of form in a game played inside a fenced area.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rusty means one's skill has declined from lack of recent practice.

clue.text: Endlessly whet top of incisor or canine

indicators.note: without its end, the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to whet a blade is to sharpen it

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter only

explanation.surface: Sharpening the tip of an incisor or a canine tooth, as a dentist might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' looks like another tooth beside 'incisor'; here it means a dog. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The shar-pei is a Chinese breed of dog with a deeply wrinkled skin.

clue.text: Men giddily at the edge in wild revel

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: only the letters at each edge of the word are used

parts.note: first and last letters only

explanation.surface: Men dancing dizzily on the brink during a riotous party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a riotous drunken party, a bout of unrestrained revelry.

clue.text: Organised filing near item for filing?

indicators.note: letters that are organised are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Office papers sorted near something for the files.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filing' looks like office paperwork; in the definition it means smoothing with a nail file.
explanation.definitionFit: A fingernail is what one shapes with an emery board, the thing being filed.

clue.text: Buffet with bagel or relish

parts.note: to buffet is to strike, as a gust of wind does
a bagel is ring-shaped, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A buffet offering bagels or a savoury relish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a meal spread; here it is a blast of wind. 'with' and 'or' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment, the relish with which one does something.

clue.text: Virtuoso pianist's record picked up

indicators.note: picked up by the ear, heard, so the word goes in by its sound

parts.note: to list is to record, set down in a list

explanation.surface: A great pianist's recording is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is 'is', a link; LISZT is pronounced like 'list'.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian composer famous as the greatest keyboard virtuoso of his age.

clue.text: Do jazzy vocals in musical with elevated finale

indicators.note: in a down entry the last letter is lifted to the top

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.surface: A singer improvises jazz vocals in a show with a rousing high ending.
explanation.walkthrough: The final S of CATS is raised to the top; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is improvised jazz singing with nonsense syllables instead of words.

clue.text: A pain to accommodate dry official on mission

indicators.note: the letters host the abstainer's letters inside them

parts.note: an ache is a pain
TT, teetotal, means not drinking, dry

explanation.surface: Putting up a teetotal official is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a diplomat posted to an embassy, an official serving abroad on a mission.

clue.text: Forms short row, with leader of soldiers on point

indicators.note: in an across entry, the soldiers' letter comes after the point
cut short, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to scull is to row a boat

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter only

explanation.surface: A short line of soldiers forms up with its leader at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forms' is a verb here: carves or shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculptor sculpts, that is shapes or models, material into figures.

clue.text: A number could be seen outside this sporting fixture?

indicators.note: the letters of seen lie around the outside of the answer within the number

parts.note: seventeen is a number
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spectator wonders if a number could be glimpsed outside the sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Put S at the front and EEN at the back of EVENT and you get SEVENTEEN: so the number is 'seen' outside this.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a single contest or race in a sports programme, a fixture.

clue.text: Today, disheartened depositor admitted to strain in chilly bank

indicators.note: the pieces are let in to the strain word

parts.note: to strain flour is to sift it
now means at present, today

indicators.note: with its heart taken out, only the outer letters remain

parts.note: first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A disheartened bank depositor is let into a strained, frosty bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' in the surface is a financial one; the definition's bank is a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowdrift is a heap of snow piled up by the wind, a cold bank.
